title: Juniper and the Colony
premise: Mirabel Ashgrove smuggles stolen memories in his own skull, running the silent route between worlds that severed contact after the Colony War. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, he discovers the flicker was a distress pulse from Juniper, a lost colony ship whose crew encoded their final memories into the relay at the edge of dead space. Racing a fleet truce that expires in eleven days, Mirabel must decide whether to deliver the Juniper's inheritance of grief and guilt to the worlds that abandoned them, or bury it forever. He broadcasts the memories, reigniting contact between the worlds at the cost of his own smuggled cargo and his freedom.
about_author: O. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space relay stations before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and a strong opinion about lighthouses.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mid-run between quarantined Halcyon and neutral Vesper Gate, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; his cargo of contraband memories nearly ruptures its containment. In the aftermath, every comm channel carries the same impossible harmonic. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine competence shattering.

chapters.title: The Harmonic
chapters.summary: Mirabel decodes the nine-second anomaly as an old Colony-era distress pattern no living ship should know. His fence, Idris Vane, offers triple pay to find its source—and quietly warns him the fleet is hunting it too. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: greed wrestling with instinct to run the other way.

chapters.title: Cargo That Bites
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashbacks in second person as he reviews his smuggled memories—stolen childhoods, war crimes, a dead sister's last day. One memory fragment resonates with the harmonic, suggesting he already carries a piece of Juniper without knowing it. Emotional beat: the past as physical weight.

chapters.title: Customs at Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: Fleet inspector Sefa Okonkwo's POV. She interrogates Mirabel but lets him pass, planting a tracker, because she suspects the signal predates the truce and could restart the war her family died ending. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience, told from the antagonist's side.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He takes the uncharted lane through debris fields of Colony War wrecks, guided by the resonating memory fragment. A near-collision with a derelict forces him to dock and scavenge, finding crew logs that name Juniper directly. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What the Wrecks Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel reading wreck logs, intercut with Okonkwo closing on his trail. The logs reveal Juniper was not lost—it was deliberately cut off by both fleets to hide an atrocity. Emotional beat: the sickening realization that survival required forgetting.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Past the last beacon, his ship's systems begin failing and the memory fragment grows vivid—he experiences Juniper's final hours as if they were his own. Isolated and half-dissolved into another life, he chooses to keep going. Emotional beat: identity dissolving into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Mirabel reaches the ancient relay and finds Juniper's full archive: ten thousand memories, including the truth that the colony voted to be erased rather than become weapons. Okonkwo arrives with guns drawn as the truce clock hits its final hours. Emotional beat: confrontation where both are right.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Mirabel's POV. With Okonkwo's weapon aimed at him, he uploads the archive to every open channel in the system—the fleet cannot stop a signal already traveling. Okonkwo must choose: shoot him and confirm the cover-up, or stand down. She stands down. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Colony
chapters.summary: Epilogue, split POV. Months later, the worlds speak again—angrily, imperfectly, but speaking—as Juniper's memories become public inheritance. Mirabel serves out a reduced sentence teaching others to carry memory honestly; Okonkwo testifies before the new joint council. Emotional beat: grief transformed into something survivable, passed on.
